::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Cubic Function and Epsilon-Delta Definition](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2518464/cubic-function-and-epsilon-delta-definition), asked by user446681 on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-11-13; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I’ve tried adding terms and construct a perfect square but failed. I’m stuck. 
>
> How can I show that this limit equals four by using epsilon-delta definition. 
>
> > $$\lim_{x\to 1} (x^3 + 4x^2 - 1) = 4$$
:::

Hint:
$$(x^3 + 4x^2 - 1)-4 = x^3 + 4x^2 - 5 = (x-1)(x^2 + 5)$$
The first factor can be made smaller than any $\delta$ you please.  What about the second?
